metadata.title: Trump: Rep. Dana Rohrabacher meets with Julian Assange for a pardon quid pro quo

existing_copy_for_context_only.short: Trump: Rep. Dana Rohrabacher meets with Julian Assange for a pardon quid pro quo
existing_copy_for_context_only.medium: Rep. Dana Rohrabacher met Julian Assange, Charles Johnson and Assange’s lawyer at Ecuador’s London embassy in August 2017. Rohrabacher later said he hoped Assange could provide evidence about the 2016 WikiLeaks releases; Assange reportedly sought assurance he would not be arrested. A Senate inquiry found no evidence supporting Rohrabacher’s or Assange’s theories. Accounts differ on whether a presidential pardon was offered or only discussed.
existing_copy_for_context_only.long: On August 16, 2017, Rep. Dana Rohrabacher met Julian Assange and activist Charles Johnson at Ecuador’s embassy in London; Assange’s lawyer was also present. The meeting concerned Assange’s offer to provide material about the 2016 WikiLeaks releases and whether Russia was involved. Rohrabacher later said he hoped the meeting could help him test his theory about how the emails were obtained. The Senate Intelligence Committee reported that Assange wanted an assurance he would not be arrested if he left the embassy and that Rohrabacher promised to ask the White House about arranging one. Rohrabacher said he was not permitted to speak with President Trump and did not communicate further with Assange about a potential deal. The committee said it found no evidence supporting Rohrabacher’s theory or Assange’s claims.
